decision_reason: Bounded state space: CODE_REGISTRY contains ~90 entries. Kani can exhaustively verify for all registered strings that from_static(s).is_some() and for unregistered strings that from_static(s).is_none(). This is a core invariant that must not panic or return invalid SymbolicCode.
Property-based testing generates arbitrary &str values and asserts from_static only succeeds for registry strings. Defense-in-depth alongside Kani verification.

No temporal behavior. SymbolicCode::from_static() is a pure lookup function over const static data. No queues, retries, leases, distributed protocols, or state machines over time. See boundary-map §2.1: Pure core has no time/concurrency.

Invariant is a const-validated data consistency check (registry lookup over ~90 entries), not algorithmic correctness needing inductive proofs. Kani handles bounded verification; proptest handles enumeration. Verus would add disproportionate engineering cost for P1 diagnostic infrastructure with no additional safety benefit over const-eval + Kani.

SymbolicCode is a simple newtype over &'static str with a const lookup validation. No complex refinement types, typestate transitions, or dependent predicates. From_static() validation is a membership check, not a refinement predicate.

No concurrency primitives in any diagnostic module. CODE_REGISTRY is a const static (&[CodeEntry]). From_static() is a pure function with no mutable state. No atomics, channels, locks, or async code. See hazard-analysis §5: Concurrency hazard severity is NONE.

No unsafe code in any diagnostic module. SymbolicCode wraps &'static str from string literals in CODE_REGISTRY — always valid 'static lifetime with correct provenance. #![forbid(unsafe_code)] is applied.

From_static() is a const lookup over a bounded set of static strings. Not an external input boundary. Fuzzing is not applicable: there is no unbounded hostile input surface. Hostile input is handled at the serde Deserialize boundary (PS-012).

Registry bijection is a critical invariant. Kani verifies at const-eval time: no duplicate symbolic names, no duplicate numeric codes. Bounded state space of 90 entries is trivially within Kani's capacity.
Runtime defense-in-depth: enumerate all registry entries, assert symbolic and numeric uniqueness via property test. Guards against registry drift not caught at compile time.
Registry is static const data — no temporal state transitions, no processes, no interleaving. See VLD-003 for full rationale.
Registry uniqueness is a const assertion, not algorithmic correctness. See VLD-004 for full rationale.
Registry is static const data defined at compile time. No external input surface for registry lookup.

Round-trip bijection is fundamental to the SymbolicCode↔DiagnosticCode mapping. Kani verifies: for every entry in registry, from_static(s).unwrap().numeric_code() == registry[s] AND DiagnosticCode(registry[s]).symbolic_code() == Some(s).
Property test: for each registry entry, assert symbolic→numeric→symbolic is identity. Combined with PS-002 bijection test.
See VLD-003. Round-trip is a pure data property, not temporal.
Round-trip is an internal bijection property with bounded input space. No hostile input surface.

ValidationError::code() must return a registered SymbolicCode for every variant. Kani verifies: for each of the ~58 variants, code() returns a SymbolicCode that is in the registry and produces a non-zero numeric code.
Exhaustive match is enforced by Rust compiler (no wildcard arm). Proptest is more appropriate for uniqueness (PS-005/PO-017). This seed's proptest value is covered by PO-017.
non_applicability_evidence_refs: contract.md#C-VE-2: 'match without wildcard arms forces compile error'

decision_reason: See VLD-004. Exhaustive match is compiler-enforced; Kani handles the value-level check.
Error variants are internal types, not an external input boundary.

58 ValidationError variants must produce 58 unique SymbolicCodes. Proptest enumerates all variants, collects codes, and asserts set size == 58. Extends existing all_variants_have_unique_diagnostic_codes test for symbolic codes.

Uniqueness check is better suited to proptest enumeration of 58 variants. Kani could do this but would duplicate the proptest obligation without adding value. PS-004 (PO-003) already covers code() registration for each variant.
Internal uniqueness property, not an external input boundary.

Kani verifies is_supported_code() accepts all numeric code constants defined across the workspace (E01xx-E06xx, E10xx-E14xx, E20xx, E30xx, E40xx+). For each constant, assert is_supported_code(CONST) == true.
Property test: parse E0501, E0601, E401C etc. and assert success. Generate E-style strings in/out of range.
See VLD-004. is_supported_code() is a const matches! expression — Kani is the natural verifier.
is_supported_code() input is bounded (E-style 5-char strings, not arbitrary). Fuzzing is not the right layer — Kani's exhaustive bounded-space check is more thorough for this finite input space.
non_applicability_evidence_refs: type-contracts.md#Section3: FromStr requires exactly 5 chars, E + 4 hex

decision_reason: Diagnostic constructor must produce records where numeric_code.symbolic_code() == Some(code). Kani proof: for any valid SymbolicCode, constructing a Diagnostic yields self-consistent symbolic/numeric fields.
Property test: construct Diagnostic for each SymbolicCode, assert code and numeric_code are consistent. Defense-in-depth for constructor invariant.
Diagnostic construction is internal, not an external input boundary.
YamlError is a new code() implementation. Kani verifies: for each of 20 YamlError variants, code() returns a SymbolicCode that is in the registry.
Covered by PS-009/PO-020 (CompileError symbolic codes) and PS-019/PO-024 (error type enumeration). YamlError 20 variants are enumerated alongside other error types.
non_applicability_evidence_refs: proof-strategy.md#Section3.3: PS-009 and PS-019 cover all error types

decision_reason: YamlError variants are internal types, not external input.

CompileError currently emits some codes not in Section 16 (e.g., UNKNOWN_INPUT_SCHEMA_FIELD). Proptest: enumerate all CompileError variants, assert code() returns SymbolicCode that is in the registry. Ensures all compilation-specific codes are registered.
Proptest enumeration of 60+ CompileError variants is the appropriate approach. Kani would duplicate without adding value.

decision_reason: Internal error variants, not external input.

Zero-allocation is a performance invariant. Kani with alloc stubs verifies no allocation path is reached during SymbolicCode construction, copy, display, or numeric code resolution. If alloc stubs are infeasible, this becomes a waiver candidate (WVR-PS010-ALLOC).
limitation_kind: Kani alloc stubs. May not detect all indirect allocation paths (e.g., Display trait format strings using std::fmt).

decision_reason: Zero-allocation is a static property, not a behavioral property suitable for proptest. Kani (or const assertion) is the appropriate tool.
Static property, not an input boundary.

Backward compatibility is a release-critical invariant. Kani: for all previously supported codes (E0101–E040C, E1001–E401B), assert from_str succeeds. For all newly added codes (E0501–E0603, E401C+), assert from_str succeeds.
Kani's bounded verification over the exact set of known codes is more precise than random generation. Covered by PO-018 (is_supported_code proptest) as defense-in-depth.
Backward compatibility is about exact known codes, not unbounded input. Kani provides more precise coverage.

Kani: for all registered symbolic strings, Serialize→Deserialize round-trips to the same SymbolicCode. For well-formed but unregistered strings, Deserialize returns Err. Bounded verification of the exact codec contract.
Property test: generate SymbolicCode from registry, serialize to string, deserialize back, assert equality. Generate arbitrary strings, assert only registry strings deserialize.
Hostile input boundary. Fuzz target: arbitrary JSON with 'code' field, assert deserialization either succeeds with valid SymbolicCode or fails with error. No panic, no undefined behavior.
See VLD-004. Serde codec boundary is inherently FFI-like and not suitable for Verus proof engineering. Kani + proptest + fuzz provide adequate defense-in-depth.
Const assertion at compile time. Kani verifies: for all entries in CODE_REGISTRY, numeric != 0. Zero is reserved sentinel for 'no error'.
Covered by PO-021 (registry category + non-zero + uniqueness combined property test).
See VLD-004. Const assertion covers this.
Static data assertion, not input boundary.
Const assertion: for each CodeEntry, (numeric >> 8) & 0xFF matches expected high-byte range for its CodeCategory. Kani verifies at const-eval time.
Runtime defense-in-depth: enumerate all registry entries, assert category consistency with numeric high byte. Combined with PS-013 non-zero and PS-002 uniqueness into unified registry property test.
Static data assertion, not input boundary.
Reverse-lookup: for each numeric code in registry, DiagnosticCode(code).symbolic_code() == Some(expected). For values outside registry, returns None. Kani verifies bounded bijection.
Property test: for each numeric code, symbolic_code() round-trip matches. For arbitrary u16 values, assert consistency.
Reverse lookup is internal, not external input.

Contract parity. Proptest: define expected mapping from master document (36 codes with symbolic names and numeric encodings), assert CODE_REGISTRY contains exact matches. Test must fail if master doc is updated but registry is not — critical regression gate.
Proptest enumeration of the expected 36-code set with assertion against master doc golden data is the appropriate approach. Kani would duplicate.

decision_reason: Determinism is critical: error codes must be stable across calls. Kani: for arbitrary error value implementing HasSymbolicCode, assert symbolic_code() returns the same result on repeated calls; never panics; no I/O.
Determinism is verified by Kani. Proptest provides additional regression but is not the primary lane for determinism invariants.
Determinism is internal, not an input boundary.

Make illegal state unrepresentable. Kani proof on Diagnostic::new() constructor: for any valid SymbolicCode, the constructed Diagnostic has numeric_code.symbolic_code() == Some(code). The derived numeric_code is deterministic from the symbolic code through registry lookup.
Constructor invariant fully covered by Kani proof (PO-014). Property test from PS-007/PO-005/PO-019 already covers the diagnostic consistency check.
Constructor is internal, not external input.
CoreError (46 variants), RuntimeError (25+), JournalError (28): each variant's symbolic_code() must return a registered SymbolicCode. Kani verifies for each variant.
Exhaustive enumeration: enumerate all CoreError, RuntimeError, and JournalError variants, assert symbolic_code() returns a SymbolicCode that is in the registry. Defense-in-depth alongside Kani.
Internal error variants, not external input.

diag_codes.rs currently #[cfg(test)] only. After promotion to public, proptest: for each of 58 numeric code constants, assert it exists in CODE_REGISTRY with correct symbolic name. Ensures no drift between constants file and registry.
Proptest enumeration of the 58 constants against the registry is the appropriate approach. Kani would duplicate without adding value.
